narrativeReportMd:
# ResearchSubject R4→R6 breaking-change assessment

## Bottom line
Breaking changes were found. The artifact identity is stable, but the local resource model is substantially remodeled: R4 `status` no longer carries subject lifecycle state in R6, R4 `individual` is renamed to `subject` and widened beyond `Patient`, R4 arm strings are replaced by `comparisonGroup`, `consent` becomes repeating, and R6 adds lifecycle and milestone backbone structures that cannot be represented losslessly in R4.

## Scope
The analysis used the local R4 and R6 core package StructureDefinitions and related local terminology artifacts. Inherited base-artifact changes from `Resource`, `DomainResource`, `Element`, and `BackboneElement` are excluded from the findings and should be handled by those base artifact reports.

## Main migration themes
The largest migration theme is that subject progress through a study moved away from a single required code on `ResearchSubject.status`. R6 uses `status` for a publication-status-like value and adds optional `subjectState` and `subjectMilestone` structures for study lifecycle details. The second theme is identity and participant generalization: R4 `individual` was a required `Reference(Patient)`, while R6 `subject` is a required reference to Patient or several non-patient entities. The third theme is representation generalization: arm names become coded or referenced comparison groups, and multiple consents can now be carried.

## Highest-impact findings
The highest-impact findings are `ResearchSubject:TERMINOLOGY_BINDING:ResearchSubject.status:4b6f2a`, because every valid R4 instance has a required status code drawn from a value set that is no longer valid for the same path in R6, and `ResearchSubject:ELEMENT_PRESENCE_OR_IDENTITY:ResearchSubject.individual:9a1c7d`, because every valid R4 instance uses a required element name that R6 replaced with `subject`.

## Findings requiring human review
Human review is needed for lifecycle-state migration, non-patient R6 subjects, arm/comparison-group mapping, and multiple consent down-conversion. The computable definitions prove the structural changes, but they do not provide a complete business mapping from old subject-status values to new publication status plus subject-state history.

## Backward-compatible design observations
Several goals appear understandable, especially support for non-patient subjects, richer state history, and multiple agreements. However, the most disruptive parts could likely have been made less breaking by preserving old element names as deprecated or transitional elements and introducing new semantics under new names rather than repurposing `status`.

## Follow-up analysis
SearchParameter changes and inherited base-resource changes should be analyzed separately. External THO terminology for R6 `subjectState` and `subjectMilestone` example bindings would improve confidence for terminology migration guidance.

summary.executiveSummaryMd: `ResearchSubject` has high-impact local breaking changes despite stable artifact identity. Top concerns are the incompatible required `status` binding and semantics, the required `individual`→`subject` element rename with widened reference targets, and the lossy replacement of arm strings with `comparisonGroup`. The main uncertainty is how HL7 intended implementations to map existing subject lifecycle states into R6 publication status plus the new lifecycle backbone elements.
summary.migrationThemesMd: Migration should treat R6 `ResearchSubject` as a remodeled resource, not just an additive version bump. R4 data needs explicit transforms for required fields (`individual` to `subject`, `status` to some combination of R6 `status` and `subjectState`) and policy decisions for data that R4 cannot carry (`subjectState`, `subjectMilestone`, non-patient subjects, multiple consents, and coded/reference comparison groups). Generated models and FHIRPath/search logic that assume R4 paths will need direct updates.
summary.confidenceSummaryMd: Confidence is high for structural, cardinality, reference-target, and required-binding changes because they are present in the local R4 and R6 StructureDefinitions and related local CodeSystems. Confidence is lower for authorial intent and exact terminology migration because no official diff, standalone narrative migration guide, or external THO expansions for the new example-bound state/milestone value sets were available.

findings.title: Required `ResearchSubject.status` was repurposed from subject lifecycle state to publication status

oldState.summary: Required code for the current state of the study subject, bound required to ResearchSubjectStatus.

binding.description: Indicates the progression of a study subject through a study.

terminologyComparison.terminologyNotesMd: The R4 ValueSet directly includes the local complete CodeSystem `http://hl7.org/fhir/research-subject-status`. No live terminology server expansion was used.

semanticText.short: candidate | eligible | follow-up | ineligible | not-registered | off-study | on-study | on-study-intervention | on-study-observation | pending-on-study | potential-candidate | screening | withdrawn
semanticText.definition: The current state of the subject.

oldState.narrativeMd: In R4 every `ResearchSubject` must carry a lifecycle state such as `candidate`, `screening`, `on-study`, `follow-up`, or `off-study`.

newState.summary: Required code for publication status of the resource, bound required to PublicationStatus.

binding.description: Codes that convey the current publication status of the research study resource.

terminologyComparison.terminologyNotesMd: The R6 ValueSet directly includes the local complete CodeSystem `http://hl7.org/fhir/publication-status`. The R4 subject-state codes and R6 publication-status codes have no overlapping code values.

semanticText.definition: The publication state of the resource (not of the subject).

newState.narrativeMd: In R6 the same required path instead carries a publication status such as `draft`, `active`, `retired`, or `unknown`; the definition explicitly says it is not the subject's status.

facts.note: Binding strength is unchanged, so the value-set replacement is directly validation-significant.

facts.oldValue: The current state of the subject.
facts.newValue: The publication state of the resource (not of the subject).

structuredDelta.matchingRationaleMd: The path and element id are identical in both versions, but the binding name, value set, allowed codes, short text, and definition all changed.

impact.impactRationaleMd: This is a hard validation break because `ResearchSubject.status` is mandatory in both versions and the required value set was replaced with a disjoint code set. Existing R4 instances with normal subject lifecycle values such as `on-study` become invalid against R6 at the same path. Conversely, an R6 instance with `status: active` uses a value that is not valid for R4 `ResearchSubject.status`. Runtime risk is high for generated enums, switch statements, analytics, and workflow rules that interpret `status` as the participant's state rather than publication state.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: Misinterpreting publication status as enrollment or treatment status could affect trial operations, reporting, cohort selection, and safety follow-up workflows.

justification.inferredGoal: Separate publication status from detailed subject lifecycle state and support richer state history through new R6 elements.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Keep `status` as the subject lifecycle state and add a separately named optional publication-status element while adding richer lifecycle history.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: The R6 goal is reasonable: publication metadata and detailed subject-state history are different facts from a single current lifecycle code. The breakage level is not clearly reasonable because R6 repurposes a required, modifier, required-bound field to a disjoint code system and meaning. A less-breaking base design could have kept old lifecycle semantics at `ResearchSubject.status` and introduced publication status under a new name.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: The strongest alternative is to retain R4 `ResearchSubject.status` for current subject lifecycle state, add optional `subjectState`/`subjectMilestone` for richer history, and add a new optional publication-status element if resource-publication state is needed. This preserves most R4-valid instances and generated enum behavior. The tradeoff is some model redundancy and the need for rules explaining how the coarse current status relates to state history, but that is a moderate cost compared with invalidating every normal R4 status value.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: The alternative preserves R4 instances but requires consistency guidance between current lifecycle status, lifecycle history, and publication metadata.

evidence.detail: R4 status is required, isModifier, summary, and bound required to ResearchSubjectStatus.
evidence.quote: The current state of the subject.

evidence.detail: R6 status is required, isModifier, summary, and bound required to PublicationStatus.
evidence.quote: The publication state of the resource (not of the subject).

evidence.detail: The R4 status code system contains subject lifecycle codes including candidate, screening, on-study, follow-up, off-study, and withdrawn.
The R6 status value set uses publication-status codes draft, active, retired, and unknown.

examples.examplesMd: The examples are illustrative fragments. A complete migration cannot infer publication status mechanically from R4 subject status without local policy; the shown `active` value is a plausible resource-publication default, not a normative mapping.

findings.narrativeMd: `ResearchSubject.status` kept the same path but changed meaning and terminology domain. This is more dangerous than a simple rename because old code continues to see a `status` property while its semantics are no longer the same. R4 implementations commonly drive enrollment, follow-up, and operational logic from this required field; in R6 those values are invalid and the closest lifecycle information is now distributed into `subjectState` and `subjectMilestone`.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: An R4-valid instance with `status: on-study` or any other R4 ResearchSubjectStatus code is invalid in R6 because the binding is still `required` but points to PublicationStatus. A valid R6 instance with `status: active` is likewise invalid in R4. Generated enum types, database constraints, FHIRPath expressions, search filters, and decision logic must be updated; leaving old code in place risks semantically wrong but syntactically successful processing if validation is weak.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Do not map R4 status values directly into R6 `status` without a business rule for publication status. Preserve the old subject lifecycle state in `subjectState.code` where possible, with `subjectState.startDate` if known; if dates are unavailable, use extensions, provenance, or a migration exception policy rather than inventing unsupported dates. Test every R4 status code, unknown or local extensions around status, and downstream workflows that use status as an enrollment-state filter.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: This was probably avoidable at the wire-format level. The R6 model could have added a new publication-status element and deprecated or complemented the old `status` field. Repurposing a required, required-bound field maximizes validation and runtime breakage and makes automated migration dependent on local policy rather than a simple structural transform.
findings.reviewerNotesMd: Reviewers should look for any official R6 rationale or migration notes explaining why a non-canonical resource uses PublicationStatus at `ResearchSubject.status`.

findings.title: Required `individual` was renamed to required `subject` and widened beyond Patient

semanticText.definition: The record of the person or animal who is involved in the study.

oldState.narrativeMd: R4 requires `ResearchSubject.individual` and restricts it to a Patient reference.

newState.summary: Required `subject` reference to Patient or several non-patient resource types.

semanticText.short: Who or what is part of study
semanticText.definition: The record of the person, animal or other entity involved in the study.

newState.narrativeMd: R6 requires `ResearchSubject.subject` and allows a broader set of participant or object resource types.

facts.oldValue: The record of the person or animal who is involved in the study.
facts.newValue: The record of the person, animal or other entity involved in the study.

structuredDelta.matchingRationaleMd: Both elements are required, summary references representing who or what is in the study; R6 keeps Patient as one target and generalizes the path name from `individual` to `subject`.

impact.impactRationaleMd: Every valid R4 `ResearchSubject` has `individual`, but R6 requires `subject` instead. A strict R6 validator rejects the old property as unknown and also reports missing `subject`. R6 instances whose `subject` references anything other than Patient cannot be represented in R4 without extension or information loss. Runtime risk is high because generated classes, FHIRPath expressions, JSON serializers, search logic, and database columns need a property-name change.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: Incorrect participant mapping can attach research participation to the wrong patient, group, specimen, device, or product, with downstream consent and reporting implications.

justification.inferredGoal: Generalize ResearchSubject so the subject of research can be a person, group, specimen, device, medication, substance, or biologically derived product.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Retain the R4 `individual` element name and widen its allowed targets and definition to cover non-patient research subjects.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: The goal of allowing research about patients, groups, specimens, devices, medications, substances, and products is well supported by the R6 target list. The hard rename from required `individual` to required `subject` was not necessary to achieve that target-domain generalization. Living with the older name plus a clearer definition would have preserved R4 Patient instances while still allowing the broader R6 model.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: A less-breaking base design could have kept `ResearchSubject.individual` as 1..1 `Reference(Patient | Group | Specimen | Device | Medication | Substance | SubstanceDefinition | BiologicallyDerivedProduct)` with short/definition text explaining that the element may identify a person, animal, group, specimen, device, or product. This avoids duplicate same-resource fields and preserves R4 wire format. The downside is terminology clarity: `individual` is awkward for groups and material objects, and search/API names would remain less aligned with other FHIR `subject` patterns.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Keeping the old name preserves wire compatibility but leaves a less precise name for groups, specimens, devices, and products.

evidence.detail: R6 `subject` is 1..1 Reference(Patient | Group | Specimen | Device | Medication | Substance | SubstanceDefinition | BiologicallyDerivedProduct).

examples.examplesMd: For Patient subjects, the structural rename is straightforward. For non-Patient R6 subjects, R4 has no target-compatible `individual` representation.

findings.narrativeMd: The participant element was not merely widened; it was renamed. Existing R4 JSON/XML instances and generated models use `individual`, while R6 requires `subject`. The target-domain widening is forward-looking, but it also means an R6 `ResearchSubject` can describe research about a group, specimen, device, medication, substance, or biologically derived product that an R4 base instance cannot carry at the corresponding required path.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: A strict R6 validator will reject an R4 instance containing `individual` and no `subject`. A strict R4 validator will reject R6 `subject`, and even a rename transform is only valid when the target is Patient. Code generators will change property names and allowed target unions, so compile-time and runtime failures are likely in clients that manipulate research subjects.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: For R4→R6, rename `individual` to `subject` and preserve the Patient reference. For R6→R4, only Patient subjects can be mapped cleanly to `individual`; non-Patient subjects need an extension, profile-specific representation, or rejection from R4 down-conversion. Tests should cover Patient, Group, and at least one material-object subject such as Specimen or Device.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: The broader target domain is probably justified by the root definition's move from a physical entity to a participant or object. The wire-level rename was only partially avoidable: keeping `individual` would be misleading for non-individual subjects, but a deprecated alias or transitional extension could have reduced breakage for existing patient-based studies.
findings.reviewerNotesMd: SearchParameter follow-up is important: R4 has `individual` and `patient` search parameters, while R6 has `subject`.

findings.title: R4 arm name strings were removed and replaced by repeating `comparisonGroup` CodeableReference

oldState.summary: Two optional string elements captured expected and actual study arm names.

semanticText.short: `assignedArm`: What path should be followed; `actualArm`: What path was followed
semanticText.definition: Assigned and actual arm names for the subject in the study.

oldState.narrativeMd: R4 allowed `assignedArm` and `actualArm` as separate `0..1` string values.

newState.summary: A repeating CodeableReference(Group) captures comparison groups used for administration or analysis.

binding.description: Example values for defining comparison groups.

semanticText.short: A group to which the subject is assigned
semanticText.definition: A group to which the subject is assigned. This group assignment is used for administration or analysis.
semanticText.comment: This grouping is used for study administration (such as assignment to arms in a trial) or study analysis (such as groupings for observational studies or sensitivity analyses).

newState.narrativeMd: R6 has no `assignedArm` or `actualArm`; it uses repeating `comparisonGroup` values that may be coded concepts or references to Group.

structuredDelta.matchingRationaleMd: `comparisonGroup` has BRIDG mapping overlap with the old arm elements and its definition covers assignment to study administration or analysis groups. It does not explicitly preserve the old assigned-versus-actual distinction, so the match is semantically plausible but not lossless.

impact.impactRationaleMd: Any R4 instance that contains `assignedArm` or `actualArm` contains elements that are absent from the R6 StructureDefinition and will fail strict validation. R6 `comparisonGroup` can repeat, can carry coded concepts, and can reference Group resources, none of which maps cleanly to the two R4 strings without deciding whether each group is assigned, actual, analytical, or observational.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: Arm and group assignment can drive intervention administration, stratified analysis, and reporting; losing the assigned/actual distinction may change interpretation.

justification.inferredGoal: Generalize trial arm strings into coded or referenced comparison groups usable for trial administration and observational analysis.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Add `comparisonGroup` while retaining deprecated `assignedArm` and `actualArm`, or add typed assigned/actual comparison-group fields.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: The R6 direction is reasonable because coded or referenced comparison groups are more computable and broader than two free-text trial-arm strings. A less-breaking design exists, but it would keep legacy strings or add parallel assigned/actual group fields alongside the generalized model. Those alternatives preserve some R4 data but carry material duplication, ambiguity about assigned versus actual versus analysis group use, and long-term interoperability cost.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: The best less-breaking option would have kept `assignedArm` and `actualArm` as deprecated optional strings while adding `comparisonGroup`, with guidance for mapping arm labels into coded concepts or Group references. Another option would be explicit `assignedComparisonGroup` and `actualComparisonGroup` elements. Both reduce immediate validation breakage, but both risk multiple indefinitely supported ways to express arm/group membership and require rules for conflicts when old strings and new groups disagree.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Retaining old arm fields preserves common R4 data but creates overlapping same-resource representations and unresolved consistency rules.

evidence.detail: R6 `comparisonGroup` is optional repeating CodeableReference(Group), example-bound to ExampleComparisonGroup.
The local R6 example comparison group CodeSystem includes example concepts such as placebo, absence-of-exposure, and usual-care.

examples.examplesMd: The migration example preserves the arm label as text but does not preserve whether the value was assigned versus actual unless an extension, coding convention, or profile rule is added.

findings.narrativeMd: R4 represented arm participation with two simple optional strings: one for the arm the subject was expected to follow and one for the arm actually followed. R6 removes both paths and introduces a more general repeating `comparisonGroup`. This is useful for richer study designs, but old arm data is invalid at the original paths and the old distinction is not obviously represented in the base R6 element.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: R4 instances containing either arm field become invalid under strict R6 validation because those element names are gone. R6 instances using multiple comparison groups, coded concepts, or Group references cannot be projected back into R4's two strings without policy choices and possible data loss. Generated R4 clients with `assignedArm`/`actualArm` properties will not align with R6 generated clients exposing `comparisonGroup` as an array of CodeableReference.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Inventory actual use of `assignedArm` and `actualArm`. If a single assigned arm is present, it can often become `comparisonGroup.concept.text` or a coded concept, but preserve assigned/actual semantics with an extension or profile if they matter. If both assigned and actual are present and differ, manual review or a project-specific mapping is needed. Down-conversion from R6 should reject or extension-carry multiple/reference comparison groups rather than silently choosing one string.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: The change is partially avoidable. Adding `comparisonGroup` could have been done without removing the old strings immediately, but preserving both models would require consistency rules and might discourage migration to coded Group-based analysis. The base R6 model favors generality over wire compatibility.
findings.reviewerNotesMd: Confirm with domain experts whether `comparisonGroup` is intended to replace both assigned and actual arms or only one of those use cases.

findings.title: `ResearchSubject.consent` now repeats

semanticText.definition: A record of the patient's informed agreement to participate in the study.

oldState.narrativeMd: R4 allowed at most one consent reference.

semanticText.definition: Agreement to participate in a study as well as other research agreements, e.g. to acknowledge additional risks, to agree to a protocol deviation, or to agree to more invasive validation subsidies.

newState.narrativeMd: R6 allows multiple consent references and broadens the description to additional research agreements.

facts.oldValue: A record of the patient's informed agreement to participate in the study.
facts.newValue: Agreement to participate in a study as well as other research agreements, e.g. to acknowledge additional risks, to agree to a protocol deviation, or to agree to more invasive validation subsidies.

structuredDelta.matchingRationaleMd: The path and target resource are unchanged; only maximum cardinality and descriptive scope changed.

impact.impactRationaleMd: This is not an R4→R6 validation break because every R4 instance with zero or one consent remains within R6 cardinality. It is a code-generation and down-conversion break: R6 generated models expose a list/array where R4 clients often expect a scalar, and an R6 instance with two or more consents cannot be represented in the R4 base element without dropping or externalizing references.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: Dropping additional consent or agreement references can lose evidence of risk acknowledgements, protocol deviations, or other research permissions.

justification.inferredGoal: Allow multiple consent and research agreement records for a single research subject.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Not applicable: increasing max cardinality from `1` to `*` preserves R4-valid instances for this element.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: The goal is reasonable because the R6 definition explicitly covers multiple consent and research-agreement records. This is not a breaking R4-to-R6 base-design issue for instances: every R4 instance with zero or one `consent` still fits the R6 cardinality. The change is primarily a runtime/model-shape and R6-to-R4 representability concern.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: A separate `additionalConsent` element could reduce scalar-to-list churn for generated clients, but under the calibration rules that is not a backward-compatible alternative to an R4-to-R6 validation break because no such validation break exists. It would also make consumers inspect two locations for consent-like agreements and would still need policy for down-converting multiple R6 agreements to R4.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: The tradeoff is generated scalar-to-list API churn and R6-to-R4 down-conversion loss, not old-valid/new-invalid base validation breakage.

examples.examplesMd: The examples focus on the `consent` fragment. A complete R6 instance with more than one consent needs an R4 down-conversion policy.

findings.narrativeMd: `ResearchSubject.consent` is a classic max-cardinality widening. It does not invalidate old R4 data, but it changes the shape of generated R6 models and permits data that the R4 base resource cannot carry. The R6 definition also broadens the element from a patient's informed agreement to participation and other research agreements.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: R4→R6 validation is safe for this element. R6→R4 is lossy when more than one consent reference exists. Runtime risk appears when client code, serializers, database schemas, or mapping templates treat `consent` as a scalar in one version and a collection in the other.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: For R4→R6, wrap any existing single `consent` in an array/list in generated model code. For R6→R4, define a deterministic selection rule only if one consent is clearly primary; otherwise carry extras in extensions or reject down-conversion. Test zero, one, and multiple consent references.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: The widening is largely justified and less disruptive than many alternatives because it keeps the same path and target. A separate extra-consents element might reduce API churn but would complicate consumers and still need R6-to-R4 policy for multiple agreements.
findings.reviewerNotesMd: Confirm whether all R6 `consent` references are semantically equivalent or whether profiles distinguish primary informed consent from other research agreements.

findings.title: R6 adds subject lifecycle and milestone backbone structures not present in R4

oldState.summary: No local backbone elements for subject state history or milestones; lifecycle was mainly represented by required `status` and optional `period`.

newState.summary: Optional repeating backbones for state intervals and milestone events, each with required coded child content when present.
newState.narrativeMd: R6 adds `subjectState` 0..* with required `code` and `startDate`, plus optional `endDate` and `reason`; it also adds `subjectMilestone` 0..* with required `milestone`, optional `date`, and repeating `reason`.

facts.note: New coded children use example bindings rather than required bindings.

structuredDelta.matchingRationaleMd: These are new local R6 elements with no same-path R4 counterpart. They are related to the R4 status lifecycle domain but are structurally new.

impact.impactRationaleMd: The new backbones are optional, so they do not make R4 instances invalid in R6 by themselves. They do create a high R6→R4 representability risk because R4 has no local structure for multiple state intervals, start/end dates per state, state-change reasons, milestones, or multiple milestone reasons. Runtime risk is medium because generated R6 models add nested components and FHIRPath/search logic may move from a single status code to collections.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: State intervals and milestone reasons can affect eligibility, protocol adherence, adverse-event windows, and study reporting.

justification.inferredGoal: Represent longitudinal subject state and milestone information that a single R4 status code could not capture.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Not applicable: optional R6 `subjectState` and `subjectMilestone` additions do not invalidate R4 instances.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: The inferred goal of representing dated subject states, milestones, and reasons is reasonable, and optional base elements are a proportionate way to support that data. By themselves these additions preserve R4-to-R6 instance compatibility because R4 instances can omit them. The compatibility problem is that R6 can now carry richer lifecycle history that base R4 lacks.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: Standard R4 extensions or external event resources can mitigate down-conversion, but those are backport and migration strategies rather than less-breaking base R6 alternatives. Since the R6 elements are optional additions, there is no old-valid/new-invalid base-design break to avoid here; the separate `status` finding covers the avoidable part of the lifecycle remodel.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: The tradeoff is R6-to-R4 representability and migration policy for richer lifecycle history, not a less-breaking R6 base design for old data.

evidence.detail: Each `subjectState` has required CodeableConcept `code` with example binding to `http://terminology.hl7.org/ValueSet/research-subject-state`.
R6 adds `subjectMilestone` 0..* BackboneElement with required `milestone` CodeableConcept when present.

possibleR6SubjectState.startDate: date required by local migration policy

examples.examplesMd: The R6 fragment cannot be represented in base R4 except by extensions or external resources. Migration from R4 status to R6 `subjectState` is not fully mechanical because R6 requires `startDate` when a state repetition is created.

findings.narrativeMd: R6 adds a new lifecycle submodel with state intervals and milestone events. This is not a hard old-data validation break because the containers are optional, but it is central to understanding the `status` change: subject progression is no longer just a required primitive code. The required children inside the optional backbones also mean migrations should not create empty `subjectState` entries just to preserve an old R4 code unless a start date is known or a local policy supplies one.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: R4 instances remain valid with respect to these additions if the new elements are absent. R6 instances that use them cannot be represented in R4 base JSON/XML at the same paths. Strict R4 parsers reject the elements, and lossy transforms would have to collapse many dated events into a single R4 `status` and `period`, losing reasons and history.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: For R4→R6, create `subjectState` only when the migration source has enough date information or a documented policy for state start dates. Preserve richer lifecycle history from source systems directly in the new backbones where available. For R6→R4, use extensions or reject down-conversion when state history or milestones matter. Tests should include absent backbones, a state with missing start date, multiple states, and milestone reasons.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: The additions themselves are reasonably backward-compatible for R4→R6 because they are optional. The lack of R4 representation is unavoidable for genuinely new lifecycle-history data unless R4 extensions are standardized. The bigger compatibility issue is the simultaneous repurposing of `status`, covered in the separate status finding.
findings.reviewerNotesMd: The example-bound THO value sets for subject state, state-change reason, and subject milestones were not locally available for expansion comparison.

checkedNoMaterialChange.notesMd: The R6 StructureDefinition is present and retains the same canonical URL, id, name, kind, type, abstract flag, derivation, and `DomainResource` baseDefinition. Metadata status changed and is reported as a notable non-breaking change.

`ResearchSubject.study` remains `Reference(ResearchStudy)` and `ResearchSubject.consent` remains `Reference(Consent)`. The material target-domain change for `individual`/`subject` is covered in a finding.

No ResearchSubject-specific invariant was found to be added, removed, or strengthened. `dom-*`, `ele-1`, and extension constraints are inherited/base constraints and are out of scope for this artifact report.
For local ResearchSubject elements, `status` remains a modifier and the other local elements checked are not modifiers. Inherited modifier-extension flag behavior is out of scope.

The comparable local summary elements remain summary elements: `identifier`, `status`, `period`, `study`, and the participant reference (`individual` in R4, `subject` in R6). Consent and the new lifecycle/comparison elements are not summary. Inherited summary flag changes are out of scope.
No fixed value, pattern value, or default value constraint was found on local ResearchSubject elements in either version.
No maxLength, minValue, maxValue, or regex value-limit change was found on local ResearchSubject elements.
No local slicing definitions were found on ResearchSubject elements in either StructureDefinition.

Types for unchanged local paths `identifier`, `status`, `period`, `study`, and `consent` are stable. Type/domain changes for the participant element and arm/comparison-group replacement are covered in findings.

nonBreakingNotableChanges.title: Artifact metadata changed from draft/trial-use to active/normative
nonBreakingNotableChanges.whyNotBreakingMd: This changes conformance and maturity metadata, not the instance wire format by itself. It does not make an R4 instance invalid or an R6 instance unrepresentable without the element-level changes reported separately.
nonBreakingNotableChanges.migrationAwarenessMd: Governance, validation policy, and product documentation may treat R6 `ResearchSubject` as more stable or normative, but the local FMM extension in the ballot package is `0`, so reviewers should rely on official HL7 status guidance if this matters.

nonBreakingNotableChanges.title: Root definition broadened from physical entity to participant or object
nonBreakingNotableChanges.whyNotBreakingMd: The root text change alone is not a validation change. The concrete breaking effect appears through the `individual`→`subject` remodel and widened reference targets, which are reported as a finding.
nonBreakingNotableChanges.migrationAwarenessMd: Business rules that assumed every ResearchSubject is a patient-like physical entity should be reviewed for R6 object subjects such as Specimen, Device, Medication, or Substance.

nonBreakingNotableChanges.title: New coded R6 elements use example-strength bindings
nonBreakingNotableChanges.whyNotBreakingMd: Example-strength bindings do not require instances to use the supplied value sets, so they are not hard validation breaks for alternative local codes.
nonBreakingNotableChanges.migrationAwarenessMd: Even though the bindings are weak, interoperable migration should prefer published codes where available or carry text/coding provenance clearly when source statuses and milestones do not match the examples.

followUpDependencies.reasonMd: Resource model changes imply search changes: R4 has `individual`, `patient`, and `date` search parameters, while R6 has `subject` and `subject_state`. These are outside this resource StructureDefinition report but important for server/client migration.
Inherited changes to base elements, constraints, language binding, and summary flags were intentionally excluded and should be covered by base artifact analyses.
These R6 example-bound ValueSets are referenced by new lifecycle and milestone elements but were not present in the local R6 core package. Expansions would improve code-level migration guidance.

analysisLimitations.descriptionMd: No official R4→R6 diff, change proposal, or migration rationale was available in the local inputs. The report infers intent from StructureDefinition definitions, bindings, and related terminology only.
analysisLimitations.whatWouldResolveItMd: An official HL7 change note or rendered diff explaining the ResearchSubject remodel would improve confidence in justification and recommended mappings.

analysisLimitations.descriptionMd: The status comparison used local complete CodeSystems, but no terminology server expansion was performed. External THO value sets for the new R6 lifecycle/milestone example bindings were not included in the core package.
analysisLimitations.whatWouldResolveItMd: Run expansions against the matching THO package/version and compare displays, definitions, and any maps to R4 research-subject-status.

analysisLimitations.descriptionMd: No local example instances with `resourceType: ResearchSubject` were found in the searched package files, and no real-world corpus was supplied. Expected prevalence is therefore based on cardinality and likely usage rather than measured data.
analysisLimitations.whatWouldResolveItMd: Analyze production or representative R4 ResearchSubject instances for use of arm fields, consent, and status values.

analysisLimitations.descriptionMd: The new artifact is from the R6 6.0.0-ballot4 build. Ballot content can still change before final publication.
analysisLimitations.whatWouldResolveItMd: Re-run the assessment against the final R6 core package when available.
